title: What is known about 1RB1LB_1RC1LD_1LA1RE_1RD0LA_0RB0RF_0RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LB_1RC1LD_1LA1RE_1RD0LA_0RB0RF_0RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At the visits of the head (state A) to the left end the tape is A>0 P (110)^N 1 with a short word P; N grows by about 3/2 per visit (…, 1080, 2457, 3690, 8325, 12492, 28122). Lean proves the eleven shift rules of the sweeps; the map is only observed.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,763 cells have been visited and 35,516 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.049). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Eleven rules over words of 1–3 cells, each for every n and every tape around; e.g. F turns (011)<sup>n</sup> into (110)<sup>n</sup> going right, D turns (111)<sup>n</sup> into (110)<sup>n</sup> going left.

claims.title: The samples
claims.text: Visits of the left end in state A on a 0 (step: tape): 6,250,987: 0 a^7 1 0 1 0 a^1080 1; 32,338,359: 0 a 1 0 1 0 a^2457 1; 73,227,424: 0 a^3 1 0 1 0 a^3690 1; 373,255,331: 0 a^8325 1; 841,543,081: 0 a 1 0 1 0 a^12492 1; 4,268,612,169: 0 a 1 0 a^2 1 0 a^28122 1 (a = 110). Consecutive ratios of N are 1.5 or 1.5² (a visit skipped).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the exact map (N, P) → (N', P') is not extracted, so the halting condition (F reading 1) is not reduced.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LF_1LC1RD_1RA1LA_0RA0RE_0RC---_1RF0LC up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LE_1LC1RC_1LA1RD_1LD0RB_0LC0LF_0LB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is a long run of the 3-cell word 110 that grows by half again between visits of the left end, while a short word at the left end keeps changing: the signature of a Collatz-like map.

facts.text: Growth of the run of 110 per visit of the left end.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.049). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,763 cells (21 left of the start, 32,353 right), with a density of 1s of 0.793.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A long run of 110
html: With a = 110, when the head reaches the left end in state A the tape is a short word followed by a long run: at step 841,543,081 it is A>0 a 1 0 1 0 a^12492 1, at step 4,268,612,169 A>0 a 1 0 a^2 1 0 a^28122 1. In between, the head sweeps the run, turning blocks of it into runs of 1s and back (the shift rules over 110, 011, 101, 111 are proved in Lean).

From one sample to the next N goes to about 3N/2 (12492 → 18738 would be one step; 28122 = 12492 · 2.25 is two), and the short left word, with counts 1 to 7, changes each time: the same picture as other Collatz-like holdouts, where that word acts as a counter fed by remainders of N.

sections.heading: Open
html: The halting transition is F reading 1. Reducing it needs the exact sample map, which has not been extracted.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1LF_1LC1RD_1RA1LA_0RA0RE_0RC---_1RF0LC: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→F, E→D, F→E; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB1LE_1LC1RC_1LA1RD_1LD0RB_0LC0LF_0LB---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A long run of the word 110 that grows by a factor of about 3/2 from one visit of the left end to the next (a Collatz-like 3n/2 map), with a short left-end word of small counts that changes at each visit.
